name: Doxycycline
route_note: Oral tablets or capsules, usually once or twice daily with water and upright posture; IV formulation available.
targets: 16S rRNA of the 30S ribosomal subunit (aminoacyl-tRNA A site)

discovery.note: A semi-synthetic tetracycline derived from oxytetracycline, with better absorption and a longer half-life.

tagline: Versatile tetracycline for atypical, tick-borne and sexually transmitted infections
summary: Doxycycline is a long-acting semi-synthetic tetracycline introduced by Pfizer in 1967. It is used for a wide range of infections including rickettsial disease, Lyme disease, chlamydia, atypical pneumonia and anthrax, for malaria prophylaxis and acne, and since 2024 as post-exposure prophylaxis against bacterial STIs in some guidelines.
mechanism: Doxycycline binds the 30S ribosomal subunit and blocks attachment of aminoacyl-tRNA to the A site, inhibiting protein synthesis; it is bacteriostatic and also active against intracellular organisms such as Chlamydia, Rickettsia and Coxiella.

At sub-antimicrobial doses it inhibits matrix metalloproteinases, the basis of its use in periodontitis and rosacea. Resistance is mainly via Tet efflux pumps (TetA, TetB) or ribosomal protection proteins (TetM, TetO). Its antimalarial effect targets the parasite's apicoplast.
uses: Rickettsial infections (Rocky Mountain spotted fever, typhus, scrub typhus)
Lyme disease and other tick-borne infections
Malaria prophylaxis and, with quinine or artesunate, treatment
Anthrax, plague, cholera, brucellosis and leptospirosis
Doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis (doxy-PEP) for bacterial STIs

history.title: Tetracycline class
history.detail: Benjamin Duggar at Lederle discovers chlortetracycline, the first tetracycline (reported 1948).

history.title: Anthrax letters
history.detail: Doxycycline and ciprofloxacin are used for post-exposure prophylaxis after the US anthrax attacks.

history.title: Price spike
history.detail: US generic doxycycline prices rise sharply amid shortages, prompting congressional scrutiny.

history.title: DoxyPEP trial
history.detail: An NEJM trial shows doxycycline taken within 72 hours after sex reduces syphilis, chlamydia and gonorrhoea in men who have sex with men and transgender women.

history.title: CDC doxy-PEP guidelines
history.detail: The US CDC publishes guidelines recommending doxy-PEP for certain populations.

pk.metabolism: minimal; enhanced clearance with enzyme inducers

serious: Tooth discolouration and enamel hypoplasia when given repeatedly in young children (lower risk than older tetracyclines)

facts: Unlike older tetracyclines, doxycycline can be used in renal impairment because it is largely eliminated by non-renal routes.
US guidance now supports short courses of doxycycline in children of any age for suspected rickettsial disease.

references.title: CDC Clinical Guidelines on the Use of Doxycycline Postexposure Prophylaxis (MMWR 2024)
